why: I checked every verifier PASS/FAIL condition against its expect line. Checks 1–3 cover the behaviour lines and each one runs the CLI (`node $B ...`, piped stdin, exit codes, a stdout diff against single-file runs); none passes a behaviour line by reading the code alone. Their conditions only test what the lines say: the `<file>:<line>: <error>` format, file order, `-` naming, exit codes 0/1/2, and that stderr has "a message" with no exact wording. Check 4 (empty diff of index.js) and Check 5 (reading the tests and README) read files, but they cover lines 4–5, not lines 1–3. Check 6 requires one PR, the Closes text and green checks, which is no stricter than line 6. Neither brief adds a branch-name rule or a mutation test. The builder's suggested stderr text ("jsonl-lint: cannot read") is guidance, not a check. Changes outside the package are only advisory ("not pass/fail"), so no file-scope limit is enforced.
